q1: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(2)>=5
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(2)>=5
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are semantically equivalent. Both queries group the COURSES table by CLASS and use a HAVING clause to filter groups where the count of rows is at least 5. In Q1, COUNT(*) counts all rows in each group, while in Q2, COUNT(2) counts the number of non-null values in the second column of the table (CLASS), which is effectively the same as COUNT(*) in this context because CLASS is not null for any row in the table. Therefore, both queries produce the same result.
